findings.where: 375 width: nav, metrics panel, feature grid (tiles 375-00, 375-01)
findings.evidence: At 375 the logo and first link collide ("skittie.devFeatures"), "Deploy now" wraps to two lines and sits past the 375 edge, the metrics panel and the three feature cards stay three columns so "churn_90d" and "cohorts.smart" run off-screen, and the page is 531px wide. The sweep reported only the logos row as the overflow culprit.
findings.before: .feature-grid / .metric-grid: three fixed columns at every width; nav without a wrap rule
findings.after: @media (max-width: 640px) { .feature-grid, .metric-grid, .price-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr } .nav-links { gap: 12px } .nav-links a { display: none } } (or a menu button)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.10 Reflow: content must fit 320 CSS px without two-direction scrolling or overlap. Nearest curated card A11-009.

findings.where: all six CTAs: Deploy now, Start free trial, Book a demo, Get started, Start 14-day trial, Contact sales, Start your free trial →
findings.evidence: dom-1440: each is a <button type="submit"> with no href and no enclosing form (forms.json is empty), so activating any of them does nothing and they are announced as buttons although they read as navigation.
findings.after: Start free trial (and equivalents for demo, pricing tiers and contact)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and 2.1.1 Keyboard: the role must match the behaviour, and a control that does nothing fails every user.

findings.where: ghost buttons "Book a demo", "Get started", "Contact sales"
findings.evidence: Boundary is border 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.16) on a transparent fill over #08090a, about 1.5:1 against the page; it is the only cue separating these buttons from body text.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: the visual boundary that identifies a control needs 3:1.

findings.evidence: "Sarah Chen" is set in the accent #5e6ad2, the same colour used for link-like CTAs, but it is a plain span.accent, not a link.
findings.after: Set the name in the body text colour and mark up the attribution as <figcaption><cite>…</cite></figcaption> inside a <figure>
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: colour implying interactivity misleads; the attribution has no programmatic tie to the quote.

findings.evidence: Labels are snake_case identifiers read aloud letter-for-letter by screen readers: "trial_to_paid", "time_to_value", "churn_90d"; units "%" and "m" are separate coloured spans, so "9m" reads as "9 m".
findings.after:
time_to_valueTime to value

and "9m"
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 3.1.4-style clarity: code-styled labels need a readable equivalent.

strengths: Focus follows visual order (nav, hero CTAs, pricing, final CTA, footer) and the browser ring is visible on the dark ground (focus/00-on.png, 05-on.png).
Decorative logo glyph SVGs carry aria-hidden="true"; one h1 and a sensible h2/h3 outline.
not_investigated: Sweep contrast hits on #5c6370 12px mono labels (3.17:1, 3.30:1) checked against 1440-00 and 1440-01: real, not disputed.
No forms present, so error handling not applicable.
No animation in stylesheets; motion not applicable.
Keyboard operation not run live; no menus, dialogs or carousels present.
